editorial:
Charlotte Gainsbourg plays an actress cast as a witch in a movie directed by Béatrice Dalle. What starts as a normal film shoot quickly falls apart as technical problems pile up and tempers flare. The set becomes a pressure cooker of stress, ego, and confusion, pulling you into a wild behind-the-scenes nightmare. The whole thing feels raw and unfiltered, like you are standing right there on the chaotic set watching everything go wrong.

The acting is intense and natural, especially from Gainsbourg and Dalle, who feel like real people losing control. The pacing is fast and jittery, building tension without much warning. On the downside, the strobe-heavy finale can be hard to watch and the story is thin. If you enjoy experimental, artsy thrillers, this is for you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the film set completely breaks down. The lights malfunction and blast the stage with blinding strobe flashes. Charlotte's character is left tied to the stake while the crew panics and argues. Béatrice Dalle tries to keep filming but loses control. The movie ends on a blinding white screen of pure light, leaving you with the feeling that the chaos of making the film became the film itself.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves experimental thrillers and behind-the-scenes chaos.
